seed: A screenshot open in a laptop window (1200 by 720), marked up until the layers list has grown to its full height, which is what a document looks like after ten minutes of work. Pick a rectangle, a piece of text, a measurement and a magnifier in turn, and read the dock's own offsets back rather than trusting a picture. The claim, one waitFor per selection so the walk FAILS rather than reports: the section named after the thing you picked is whole on screen without anyone scrolling. Two of them have no section of their own any more: a plain rectangle lost its one row to the parts list, and an arrow's caption, head and thickness followed on 2026-09-09, so what those two claim is that the section their settings DID move into, Appearance, is whole on screen. A measurement claims the whole section like everything else, and then opens the Details fold to prove the numbers that fold away are one click from where they were.

steps.note: the document every claim below is read off: a screenshot with a measurement, four rectangles, a label and a magnifier on it, so the layers list is at its full height.

THE TEST for a rectangle. Since the parts list landed a plain rectangle has no section of its own at all: its one row, the outline width, became a part inside Appearance. So the claim is that Appearance is in dockInView whole, which is where everything a rectangle owns now is.

steps.comment: ...and the layers list you clicked in is still all there. Nothing scrolled, so the next row you want is under your hand where you left it.

steps.note: the same for a piece of text, whose own section is the tallest of the three that can fit.

THE TEST for a measurement, and the one this walk used to have to give up on: the section was 470pt tall against a 344pt slot, so no ordering could fit it. Its settings now read one to a line and its read-only numbers fold away, and the whole section is in dockInView.
and nothing was taken away: one click on Details puts From, To, Distance, Units and the exact spec line back, which is what makes the trim a fold rather than a deletion.
the same for a magnifier: the Lens tool took the zoom callout's place, so the layer is called Magnify and its rows are in the Lens section.

an arrow's caption, head and thickness moved into Appearance with every other shape setting on 2026-09-09, so an arrow is now in the same case as the rectangle above: nothing of its own to show, and Appearance whole on screen under the layers list without anybody scrolling.
